corrections.issue: Faithful to the speaker but the arithmetic does not reconcile: 8,000 round turns x 2 contracts x $6 = 9.6% (and 700 per month x 12 = 8,400 gives about 10.1%); 10.8% would need about 9,000 round turns at $12. Treat 10.8% as the speaker's rough figure, about 10% a year.
corrections.fix: Moritz: at roughly 6 dollars all-in per contract and about 8,000-9,000 round turns per million per year, execution cost is roughly 10 percent a year (he states 10.8%), a very high hurdle for the short-term strategy.
